why: A jam together with an overfilled tray usually means the paper was loaded badly.
Loose guides let the stack shift and jam.
Torn pieces left inside block the paper path.
A jam message with nothing visible points to a small scrap blocking a sensor.
Damp or curled paper sticks and jams.
Damp paper wrinkles easily.
Misloaded paper is a common cause of any jam.
Leftover scraps are a common cause of any jam.
Pickup rollers wear out on older or heavily used printers.
If the tray is not overfilled, a dirty or worn pickup roller is the likely reason paper is not pulled in.
Damp or curled paper will not pick up well.
Several sheets feeding at once suggests the separation pad is not separating them.
Separation pads wear with age.
Damp paper sticks together.
Loose guides let the paper enter at an angle.
Crooked output most often comes from the paper guides.
On a laser printer wrinkles can come from a failing fuser.
Faded laser print with a low toner message means the toner is running out.
Faded laser print is most often low toner.
Draft or economy mode deliberately prints lighter.
Ink dries in the nozzles when an inkjet sits unused.
Faded inkjet print usually means clogged nozzles or low ink.
Lines on laser printouts often come from a dirty or damaged drum or cartridge.
Streaks with a low toner warning suggest the toner is nearly gone.
Lines on inkjet printouts are classic clogged nozzles.
Marks repeating at regular spacing point to a damaged drum.
A worn drum is likely on an old printer.
Ghost images can come from a worn drum.
Ghost images can also come from a failing fuser.
Toner that rubs off was not fused to the paper, so the fuser is failing.
Smudged inkjet print is often a wrong paper type or quality setting.
Ink smears on damp paper.
Smudged toner suggests poor fusing.
The protective seal on a new cartridge stops it printing.
Blank pages right after a cartridge change point to the seal or seating.
An empty toner cartridge gives blank pages.
Blank inkjet pages often mean an empty cartridge.
Dried nozzles after a long idle period give blank pages.
A low ink message with blank pages means the ink is empty.
Fully black laser pages point to a high-voltage fault.
A missing colour on an inkjet is usually a clogged nozzle or empty colour ink.
Wrong colours can come from greyscale or wrong settings.
The printer is reporting low toner.
The printer is reporting low ink.
An offline status is usually a setting on the computer.
With USB a bad cable or port can look like offline.
A wireless printer goes offline when the network link breaks.
A router change breaks the printer's connection.
If a USB printer is not detected, suspect the cable or port.
Updates often remove or break drivers.
A wireless printer not found usually lost its network.
A dropping Wi-Fi link is a signal or network setting problem.
Jobs that never print are usually stuck in the spooler.
Jobs queue up while the printer is offline.
A driver error means the driver is missing or corrupt.
The driver broke after an update.
Strange characters mean the printer cannot interpret the data it receives.
A faulty USB cable can corrupt data.
Slow printing is commonly caused by quality settings or large files.
A weak Wi-Fi link slows data transfer.
No power may be the supply, but the socket and cable must be ruled out.
With the socket and cable ruled out, the printer's own power supply has failed.
A warning light with no other symptoms needs a general reset and check.
The warning light is probably the jam sensor.
The printer cannot read the cartridge chip.
Refilled or clone cartridges often have chips the printer rejects.
A newly fitted cartridge may be mis-seated or the wrong model.
Grinding suggests worn gears or a mechanical fault.
Gears wear out with age and heavy use.
Noise with a jam usually means the rollers are fighting an obstruction.
Burning smell, smoke or extreme heat is a safety hazard.
The print head carriage is physically blocked.
